title: You look holy…
paragraphs:
You look holy…
but heaven isn’t convinced.

You’ve mastered the language of faith.
But your heart? Still untouched.

And that tension right there…
is where most people stop reading.

Because it’s too close.
Too real.
Too exposing.

You can raise your hands in worship…
and still resist surrender.

You can quote Scripture…
and still avoid the Savior.

You can look clean in public…
while hiding decay in private.
That’s the silent danger of cultural Christianity.

It’s knowing how to say “God is good”
without ever letting Him be Lord.

It’s singing about the cross
without ever dying to self.
And here’s the part that stings:

You can be around Jesus
and still miss Him completely.
“These people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.” — Matthew 15:8
And no amount of church attendance can close it.
No amount of Christian content can fix it.

Because sin isn’t just what you do.
It’s what rules you.

Pride.
Control.
Secret habits.
Unrepented desires.

That quiet voice saying,
“I’ll follow God… but on my terms.”
And God doesn’t negotiate with sin.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23

The church kids.
The ministry leaders.
The ones who never missed a Sunday.

Because outward goodness
can still hide inward rebellion.
Some scholars interpret the Pharisees not as obvious villains, but as people who sincerely believed they were right—yet were blind to their need for grace.
God didn’t expose your emptiness to shame you.
He exposed it to rescue you.

You are more sinful than you admit…
but more loved than you can imagine.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8

While you were performing.
While you were pretending.
While you were half-in, half-out…
Christ went all the way to the cross.
“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.” — 2 Corinthians 5:17
You don’t need a better routine.
“Unless one is born again he cannot see the kingdom of God.” — John 3:3

And that only happens when you stop pretending…
and start surrendering.
This is where shame meets grace.

You know the songs
but not His voice.

You know the verses
but not His presence.

You know the system
but not the Savior.
And deep down, you feel it.
That fear you won’t say out loud:
“What if I’ve been close… but not saved?”
Jesus is not standing far from you.
Just like in that moment on the road to the cross—

Dust in His wounds.
Weight on His shoulders.
Love in His eyes.
“Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” — Matthew 11:28

Bring the fake.
Bring the pride.
Bring the hidden sin.

Will you keep the image…
or finally surrender the heart?

Will you stay “almost”…
or step into fully His?

Your sin—nailed.
Your shame—covered.
Your new life—waiting.
Pray this in your own words:

“Jesus, I’m done pretending.
I surrender everything.
Not just my image… my whole life.
Forgive me. Change me.
Be my Savior and my Lord.”
“Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.” — Romans 10:13

But as a son.
As a daughter.
As someone truly changed.
If this hit your heart, don’t ignore it.
